o1.biggest_strength: It builds the whole launch around the actual winning signal: on-feet worker Spark Ads, problem-first hooks, and a $38 90-day contribution target checked against Shopify and survey data.
o1.biggest_mistake: The day-30 blended lift read is a little overconfident unless the suggested holdout is actually used, because other channel and demand changes can still affect new customers.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make the holdout or another incrementality check part of the core plan, not a bolder optional move, and tighten a few assumptions around attribution and state selection.

o2.biggest_strength: It correctly finds the money target and creative direction: worker comfort, real feet, Spark Ads from the nurse and server, problem-first hooks, and mission only as a closing fact.
o2.biggest_mistake: The measurement and scaling plan leans more on claimed orders and broad pass/fail thresholds than on a clean Shopify/survey/incrementality read, and the Smart+ scale campaign is a bit loose for month one.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the ambiguous Smart+/scale setup with a cleaner test-to-scale structure and make the day-30 decision depend on two store-side reads against the $38 90-day break-even.

reason: Output 1 is more Monday-ready and more tightly tied to the owner's numbers, especially the budget release rules, kill thresholds, Shopify tracking, Spark Ads, and day-30 decision logic. Output 2 is strong, but it is a little less precise on attribution and scaling, which matters for deciding whether TikTok has earned more budget.
